findings.title: run_container's --windows-cross forwarding is unreachable — dispatch exits on WIN_CROSS before run_container; container-leg probe only reachable via manual docker run
findings.detail: Line 182 appends --windows-cross to the container invocation, but dispatch at 220-223 runs run_windows_cross and exits before run_container is ever reached with WIN_CROSS=1. Dead code, and the container-leg probe the usage hints at cannot be driven through the one entrypoint.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove the dead forwarding line and document the manual `docker run ... tools/ci-local.sh --in-container --windows-cross` invocation, or route --windows-cross through run_container.

findings.title: --windows-cross + --mac/--native silently discards the native suite, contradicting the 'Flag conflicts fail loudly' guard (only 2 of 3 conflicting pairs rejected)
findings.detail: WIN_CROSS+NATIVE passes both guards, then the WIN_CROSS-first dispatch runs the probe and drops the requested native 8-gate suite. The spec artifact promises conflicting flag pairs exit 2.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a WIN_CROSS+NATIVE guard that exits 2, mirroring the other two checks.

findings.title: Dockerfile.ci odin-locate pipeline lacks the workflow's `|| true` — the designed 'odin binary not found' diagnostic is unreachable under set -euo pipefail
findings.detail: Empty find result makes xargs run bare dirname (exit 1); pipefail+set -e aborts the RUN before the [ -z ] guard prints the layout dump. Build still fails (no silent pass) but the mirrored-from-workflow diagnostics are lost exactly when needed (corrupt/empty tarball).
findings.recommended_fix: Append `|| true` to the find|head|xargs pipeline, exactly like the workflow line it mirrors.

findings.title: README gate-mapping table is not 1:1 with the workflow — omits 'Install Odin' + 'Linux GUI link deps' rows (spec artifact claims 'all 11 workflow steps') and paraphrases 4 of 9 step names
findings.detail: Table has 9 rows vs the workflow's 11 non-checkout steps; the 2 setup steps are prose-only. Rows 2/4/6/8 abbreviate step names while ci-local.sh's GATES array quotes them verbatim (order + commands verified correct).
findings.recommended_fix: Add the two setup rows (mapping to the Dockerfile.ci stages) and quote ci.yml step names verbatim in the left column.

findings.title: Replica↔workflow equivalence is anchored by comments only — no durable pin on the 8-gate enumeration while this suite is the only running CI
findings.detail: The workflow grew a gate with nearly every story; with GH billing-blocked the local suite is the only verification, and a new ci.yml step not mirrored into GATES silently weakens it. Verified the lists match TODAY; the gap is the missing drift guard.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a --self-test (or lint gate) asserting GATES matches ci.yml run steps 1:1, order included; document in README.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS — every verification claim is a green run; the stop-on-fail ❌/⏭/exit-1 path (the tool's core contract) was never exercised
findings.detail: P0 100% (workflow byte-identical; 8 gates in CI order verified in code). But the failure path — ❌ summary, ⏭ skip line, exit 1 — and the docker-build-failure path have no demonstrated evidence. Happy-path-only verification for a trust tool. (I read the stop-on-fail code; it is straightforwardly correct — the gap is demonstrated evidence, plus zero durable pins.)
findings.recommended_fix: Run once with a deliberately broken gate and capture the ❌/⏭/exit-1 output in the spec's Verification section; ideally as a seeded-failure self-test.

findings.title: Host-side `--in-container` runs mislabel reality: usage hint sends users to a flag that only changes message text; success message and summary LEG label claim 'container' for host-executed runs
findings.detail: IN_CONTAINER never touches docker; on the host the windows-cross probe runs the HOST toolchain yet would print 'in-container; the --rm container discards it' (app-win.exe actually persists), and run_gates' summary prints 'linux container' for any non-native run.
findings.recommended_fix: Set a marker env in the image and derive the label/message from it (or reject --in-container outside the container); document the manual container-probe command.

findings.title: README x64-parity recipe (raw `docker run --platform linux/amd64`) bypasses the --user/--rm/bind-mount wiring that only ci-local.sh applies
findings.detail: The documented parity flow runs as root with no goldens/_reports mount and no --rm; failure bundles stay root-owned in a left-behind container — inconsistent with the README's own 'only writable host surface' guarantee.
findings.recommended_fix: Show the parity flow through ci-local.sh (e.g. DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64) or document the full docker run with -v/--user/--rm.

findings.title: Empty .odin-version passes the readability guard — false toolchain warning natively, misattributed curl 404 in the container
findings.detail: Only -r is checked, not emptiness: an empty pin warns falsely in native mode and produces a 'download//odin-linux-...' URL in the image build, blamed on network.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate the pin is non-empty after reading it in run_native and the Dockerfile RUN.

findings.title: Tracked _pr_body.md (164-line Story 5.2 PR draft) deleted — housekeeping outside the briefing's deliverables
findings.detail: Benign orphan cleanup (the minion's spec artifact discloses it), but the briefing's scope guard is local test tooling only; the deletion is unrequested and currently invisible in the PR body.
findings.recommended_fix: Call it out explicitly in the PR body as housekeeping, or drop the deletion from this PR.

findings.title: No checksum/digest pinning on base image, Odin tarball, or raylib clone — exactly parity with the workflow's own posture
findings.detail: ubuntu:24.04 mutable tag + unverified curl|tar, matching ci.yml's curl -fsSL/no-checksum posture (the parity bar — no gap BEYOND CI). Unlike CI, the local fetch is cached in an image layer, so any upstream drift persists across runs.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional hardening only: pin the base image by digest and/or verify a SHA-256 of the Odin tarball; note the parity decision in the Dockerfile comment.

findings.title: .dockerignore's 'TRACKED tree' header claim overstates: untracked files and 18MB of tracked _bmad-output ship into the image; gitignored _charter scratch pattern not mirrored (none present in this checkout — conditional exposure)
findings.detail: docker build sends the working tree minus dockerignore — not a git checkout. Verified: no _charter files and no secrets in this checkout; the artifact-poisoning isolation (the guarantee that matters) is intact. Exposure is bloat + future scratch, not a live hole.
findings.recommended_fix: Add '_bmad-output' (or '_bmad-output/**/review/') to .dockerignore mirroring .gitignore, and qualify the header claim.

findings.title: A uid-0 invoker runs the suite as root and leaves root-owned debris in the host bind mount
findings.detail: --user $(id -u):$(id -g) is correct for non-root invokers and no docker socket is exposed; but on Linux a root invoker writes root-owned files into goldens/_reports on the host.

findings.title: .dockerignore is a strict subset of .gitignore's artifact set (export/, *.dmg, *.zip, .godot/, game/tests/captures/, *.blend1 not mirrored) — no live hole, the guarantee rests on the two lists never drifting
findings.detail: Verified every current gate output (bin/, tools/raylib-sw/, goldens/_reports/, app*.bin, app-win.exe, *.dSYM) IS excluded; the unmirrored patterns are packaging/capture artifacts no gate produces. A future artifact path added to .gitignore only would silently leak into the image.
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror the remaining gitignored artifact patterns in .dockerignore, or qualify the blanket isolation claim.

findings.title: windows-cross exit-0-with-warning semantics pinned by comments only — the missing-binary check is correct today, nothing would catch its removal
findings.detail: The -s app-win.exe artifact check (the exact lie the swarm caught) has no durable test; a future edit flipping the final return 0 passes silently.
findings.recommended_fix: A stubbed-odin test of run_windows_cross (missing binary + rc 0 → warn + exit 0) wired into the proposed self-test.

findings.title: docker-down and docker-build-failure branches exist in code but appear nowhere in the verification evidence
findings.detail: The plain-language docker-down message (a lens-guard item — code verified correct) has no demonstrated run in the spec's Verification section.
findings.recommended_fix: Stop Docker once and paste the message + exit 1 into the Verification section.

findings.title: Gates execute via plain `bash -c`, not GH's `bash -eo pipefail` — latent parity gap, zero impact today (downgraded from warning)
findings.detail: Verified empirically: pipefail does NOT propagate to bash -c children. But no current gate command uses a pipeline, the && chains match -e semantics exactly, and the gate scripts carry their own set-flags (lint.sh, harness.sh) — so execution fidelity is exact TODAY. The Dockerfile's SHELL comment covers build-time RUN steps, where it is accurate. Only a FUTURE gate containing a pipeline would diverge.
findings.recommended_fix: Run gates through `bash -eo pipefail -c "$cmd"` for exact parity with GH's shell: bash defaults (one-word change, no current behavior delta).
